name: Replicate-count decision rule v1 (locked before the clean precision pilot)
recorded_utc_source: system clock (datetime.now(timezone.utc)) at the moment this file was written; not typed by hand
question: How many independent graphs are needed before the paired estimates stop changing enough to matter? Not decided by significance or by which count makes results look best.
statistical_unit: one independently generated graph instance. Timing repetitions on one graph are technical replicates (summarised by their median) and never count as replicates.
ladder_rationale: every level is a multiple of 4, so the Williams execution order keeps the four algorithms exactly position-balanced at every candidate count; constant +8 steps keep the stability comparison like-for-like

pilot.rationale: every primary geometry, both primary densities, smallest / middle / largest primary n, so high-variance regimes are caught; not the full factorial
pilot.measurement_protocol: identical to the final study: CGAL backend, Williams execution order, timing repetitions 5, warmups 1, process_mode shared, validate all
pilot.machine_conditions: clean run under the machine-preparation checklist of docs/final_experiment_protocol.md

prefix_rule: an evaluation at k uses graphs with replicate number 1..k of each cell, i.e. exactly the graphs a k-replicate study would have collected; no resampling or selection
comparisons: every unordered algorithm pair (6) in every pilot cell, paired on identical graphs, CGAL backend

cds_fraction.ci: Student-t 95% CI of the mean of d over the first k graphs: half-width = t(0.975, k-1) * sd / sqrt(k)
cds_fraction.precision_value: half-width in percentage points of CDS fraction (x 100)

runtime_ratio.per_graph: l = ln(T_A / T_B), T = median of that graph's timed repetitions
runtime_ratio.ci: Student-t 95% CI of the mean of l: half-width h = t(0.975, k-1) * sd / sqrt(k)
runtime_ratio.precision_value: multiplicative half-width m = exp(h) - 1 (e.g. 0.10 = CI within x/÷ 1.10)

strata: adequacy is judged separately in every (geometry, density) stratum of the pilot (10 strata, 3 sizes x 6 pairs = 18 comparisons each); densities are never pooled, so the count is set by the least-precise primary regime

narrowness.rule: k is narrow enough iff in EVERY stratum: >= 90% of comparisons have CDS half-width <= 1.0 pp and none exceeds 2.0 pp, AND >= 90% have runtime m <= 0.10 and none exceeds 0.20

selection: choose the smallest k in {20, 28, 36, 44, 52} that satisfies the narrowness thresholds (CDS quality and runtime) in every required pilot stratum. If even k = 52 fails, the outcome is reported explicitly as 'precision target not met at 52' with every failing comparison; 52 is NOT declared sufficient and the final experiment stops for a protocol decision.
applies_to: experiments/final.json synthetic.replicates (and the optional sparse study, which follows the final count)
write_up: Each experimental cell was evaluated on k independently generated graph instances, selected through a preregistered precision pilot (rule recorded in experiments/precision/replicate_rule_v1.json before the pilot ran).

amendments.amended_utc_source: system clock at the moment of the amendment

stability.rule: for k < 52: in EVERY stratum and for BOTH metrics, improvement = 1 - median_hw(k + 8) / median_hw(k) < 0.15 (median over the stratum's 18 comparisons; improvement = 0 when median_hw(k) = 0). At k = 52 there is no next level, so stability is not required.

amendments.reason: Under independent sampling the CI half-width scales as t(0.975,k-1)/sqrt(k), so the k -> k+8 improvement is arithmetic, not data-driven: expected 17.1% (k=20), 12.7% (28), 10.1% (36), 8.4% (44). Simulation with 18 comparisons per stratum: per-check pass probability 0.27 (k=20), 0.86 (28), 1.00 (36+); with 10 strata x 2 metrics all required, k=28 passes with probability ~0.05. The test would have made 36 the effective minimum regardless of the data and made 28 a coin flip. Owner's decision: narrowness only.

amendments.amended_utc_source: system clock at the moment of the amendment

replaced.selection: choose the smallest k in the ladder that is narrow enough (narrowness rule above, in every stratum). If no k is narrow enough, use 52 (the cap) and report every comparison that misses the narrowness thresholds at 52; no ladder value is added and no threshold is loosened.

amendments.reason: owner: no silent fallback to the cap; if 52 fails, stop for a protocol decision. Trajectory plots added as a non-binding diagnostic.

stability_diagnostic: non-binding: point-estimate trajectories (paired CDS-fraction difference and geometric-mean runtime ratio, with their CIs) are plotted across k for every comparison. They inform the write-up only and never change the selected k. A nested 'k+8 estimate inside the k CI' rule is deliberately not used: cumulative estimates at k and k+8 share observations, so it passes very frequently under ordinary noise.
